description: GloFAS (Global Flood Awareness System) daily river discharge (m³/s) for the largest modeled river within 5 km of the given coordinates — no river ID needed. That river is not always the closest one: at 5 km resolution a point near a confluence or a pair of parallel channels can resolve to an unintended reach. When the returned discharge looks unrepresentative for the intended river, Open-Meteo suggests varying the coordinate by about 0.1° and comparing the values. One mode per call: forecast_days for the outlook, or start_date and end_date together for a date range from 1984-01-01. The two modes are mutually exclusive, and a date range needs both ends — a lone start_date or end_date is rejected. forecast_days accepts up to 210, but the current GloFAS run sets how far the data reaches (about six months ahead); later days come back null and the notice names where the data ends. What a date range holds depends on the model. Omitting models reads seamless_v4: consolidated_v4 reanalysis before 2023-08-05, then forecast-run discharge from 2023-08-05 on, so a range crossing that date changes source mid-series. Set models to pin a source: seamless_v4 (default — consolidated_v4 reanalysis before 2023-08-05, forecast_v4 runs from 2023-08-05 into the live forecast), consolidated_v4 (reanalysis from 1984 through 2025-05-31; null after it and on every forecast_days call), forecast_v4 (forecast runs from 2023-06-01 into the live forecast; null before). consolidated_v4 is the only way to read reanalysis for 2023-08-05 through 2025-05-31. With 2+ models every daily column is suffixed with the model name (river_discharge_consolidated_v4). Available daily variables: "river_discharge" (the daily discharge value; the mean across ensemble members is "river_discharge_mean"), and the ensemble statistics "river_discharge_mean", "river_discharge_median", "river_discharge_min", "river_discharge_max", "river_discharge_p25" (25th percentile), and "river_discharge_p75" (75th percentile). The statistics carry spread across ensemble members on forecast-run days — the forecast_days outlook, and date-range days from 2023-08-05 under seamless_v4 or forecast_v4. On reanalysis days (seamless_v4 before 2023-08-05, consolidated_v4 through 2025-05-31) they repeat river_discharge and are not uncertainty estimates. Returns null for coordinates far from any river or in areas without GloFAS coverage. A wide date range produces thousands of daily records and spills to a DataCanvas when canvas is enabled, returning canvas_id and table_name with truncated: true — inspect the staged columns with openmeteo_dataframe_describe, then query the full set with openmeteo_dataframe_query. With canvas disabled it returns a bounded preview instead.

canvas_id.description: DataCanvas token for wide date-range queries. When a result is too large to return inline — driven by total payload size, so a multi-variable pull can spill at any row count — it spills to this canvas: pass the returned token to openmeteo_dataframe_describe to list the staged table and its columns, then to openmeteo_dataframe_query to run SQL against it. Omit to create a fresh canvas.

daily_variables.description: Daily discharge variables to fetch (e.g., ["river_discharge", "river_discharge_p25", "river_discharge_p75", "river_discharge_min", "river_discharge_max"]). Required. river_discharge is the daily discharge value; the _mean, _median, _min, _max, _p25, and _p75 statistics span the ensemble members on forecast-run days — the forecast_days outlook, and date-range days from 2023-08-05 under seamless_v4 or forecast_v4. On reanalysis days (seamless_v4 before 2023-08-05, consolidated_v4 through 2025-05-31) they repeat river_discharge and are not uncertainty estimates.

end_date.description: End of the date range (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive). Must be on or after start_date. Days from 2023-08-05 are forecast-run discharge under the default seamless_v4; consolidated_v4 reanalysis ends 2025-05-31 and answers later days with null. Requires start_date — the pair must be sent together, and neither combines with forecast_days.

forecast_days.description: Number of forecast days ahead (1–210). The API accepts up to 210, but the current GloFAS run sets how far the data reaches (about six months); later days come back null. consolidated_v4 serves no forecast days — with it every row is null. Mutually exclusive with start_date/end_date — omit it entirely when pulling a date range.

latitude.description: Latitude in decimal degrees. Discharge is returned for the largest modeled river within 5 km of this point — no river ID required, and not necessarily the closest river. Vary the coordinate by about 0.1° and compare when the result looks unrepresentative. Use openmeteo_search_locations to resolve a place name.

longitude.description: Longitude in decimal degrees. With latitude it selects the largest modeled river within 5 km, which is not necessarily the closest one.

models.description: GloFAS models to read from: seamless_v4 (default — consolidated_v4 reanalysis before 2023-08-05, forecast_v4 runs from 2023-08-05 into the live forecast), consolidated_v4 (reanalysis from 1984 through 2025-05-31; null after it and on every forecast_days call), forecast_v4 (forecast runs from 2023-06-01 into the live forecast; null before). Omit to use Open-Meteo's seamless_v4 default. With 2+ models each daily column and unit key is suffixed with the model name (river_discharge_consolidated_v4); one model keeps plain names. A model with no data for the requested days answers with null values rather than an error, and the notice names those columns. A name outside this list (the GloFAS v3 selectors included) is sent upstream rather than rejected here.

start_date.description: Start of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD, e.g., "2023-01-01"), from 1984-01-01. Under the default seamless_v4 a range holds consolidated_v4 reanalysis before 2023-08-05 and forecast-run discharge from 2023-08-05 on; request models: ["consolidated_v4"] for reanalysis through 2025-05-31. Requires end_date — the pair must be sent together, and neither combines with forecast_days.

name: openmeteo_get_flood

canvas_id.description: DataCanvas token for the staged full dataset. Present only when truncated is true AND DataCanvas is enabled (CANVAS_PROVIDER_TYPE=duckdb) — absent otherwise, in which case the preview is all this response carries. Pass to openmeteo_dataframe_describe to list the staged table and its columns, then to openmeteo_dataframe_query to run SQL against it.

daily.description: Per-day records with "time" (YYYY-MM-DD) + one key per requested variable containing discharge in m³/s — per model, suffixed with the model name (river_discharge_consolidated_v4), when 2+ models were requested — or null for coordinates outside GloFAS coverage and days the selected model does not serve. When truncated, contains only a preview — query canvas_id for the full dataset when one is present.

daily_units.description: Variable → unit string for daily data (e.g., {"river_discharge": "m³/s"}), model-suffixed like the records when 2+ models were requested.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `no_variables_requested`: daily_variables named no variable — omitted, empty, or holding only blank or whitespace-only entries. `date_range_incomplete`: Only one of start_date / end_date was provided — GloFAS requires the pair together. `forecast_days_conflict`: A start_date or end_date range was combined with a forecast_days value. `date_order_invalid`: The end_date value is earlier than the start_date value. `date_out_of_range`: start_date predates 1984-01-01 or date range is otherwise invalid. `invalid_variable`: An unknown discharge variable or model name was requested. `invalid_timezone`: timezone was blank, or upstream did not recognize the requested time zone. `request_too_large`: Open-Meteo refused the request as asking for too much data in one call. `coverage_gap`: Open-Meteo has no data at this coordinate for the requested dataset or model, because its grid or domain does not reach the point. `rate_limited`: Open-Meteo answered HTTP 429 because a free-tier request limit was reached. `upstream_unavailable`: Open-Meteo was unreachable, answered with a server error, or returned an unreadable response on all three attempts. `upstream_timeout`: Open-Meteo failed on all three attempts, and the last one got no answer within 15 seconds. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

latitude.description: Snapped latitude — grid point of the selected river

longitude.description: Snapped longitude — grid point of the selected river

models.description: GloFAS models requested — echoes the models parameter. Absent when models was omitted, which means the data came from seamless_v4: consolidated_v4 reanalysis before 2023-08-05, forecast_v4 runs from 2023-08-05 on.

notice.description: Everything this response needs to say beyond the data, composed into one advisory: columns GloFAS returned with the unit "undefined" (a name it parsed but does not serve); recognized columns whose requested days fall outside the coordinate's discharge record or the selected model's span, with the dates that do carry values; and, when the result spilled, either the canvas and table holding the full row set plus the two dataframe tools that read it, or — with DataCanvas disabled — why there is no canvas_id and how to reach the rows the preview omits.

record_count.description: Total number of daily discharge records — the full staged count when truncated is true, not the length of the daily preview.

table_name.description: DuckDB table name for the staged data — use as the FROM target in openmeteo_dataframe_query SQL; openmeteo_dataframe_describe lists its columns. Present only alongside canvas_id.

truncated.description: True when the response was too large to return inline, so daily carries a bounded preview rather than the full set. With DataCanvas enabled the complete data is staged at canvas_id. With it disabled there is no canvas_id, and the omitted rows are reached only by narrowing the request.

title: Openmeteo Get Flood
